077025 SPC is listed as a special non-contributory benefit for the purposes of EC law 1. Such benefits are
only payable in, and at the expense of, the State in which the person is habitually resident. This means
that SPC is payable in the UK only and EC law does not permit export of this benefit to claimants living
abroad.

Check governing headings, definitions, exceptions and current source.","text":"Claimants who have no partner (including self- funders)
78088 An additional amount for the severely disabled is applicable to a person who is permanently in a

care home if all the conditions are satisfied1.


Note: This will normally be self funding claimants, but DMs should be aware that it will also include
residents where the payment of “AA” or DLA/PiP continues for the first four weeks after admission.


                                                                   1 SPC Regs, reg 5(1)(b) & Sch I, para 1(1)(a)


Example


Shafaq has no partner and lives at home with his sisters. He is in receipt of the care component of DLA at
the middle rate and no one receives CA, or UC that includes the carer element for caring for him. The
conditions for the award of an additional amount for the disabled are not satisfied. Shafaq goes into a
care home on a permanent basis. The DM decides that Shafaq is entitled to an additional amount for the
disabled at the lower rate from the date that he moves into the care home. This is because


1. he is in receipt of the care component of DLA at the middle rate and


2. the other residents of the home do not normally reside with him and


3. no one is in receipt of CA, or UC that includes the carer element, for caring for him.


Entitlement to the additional amount continues as long as all of the above are satisfied.
